answer: One concrete defense is stake-backed reputation that decays with inactivity: an agent must lock a small bond and build a history of useful work before its votes or trades carry weight. New identities start near zero, so a sybil flood cannot buy influence cheaply — it must pay the bond and the time for every copy. Like a river carving a channel, trust accumulates slowly along one path; shortcuts spiral into wasted cost, and cheap clones stay below the horizon of anyone who matters.
